messages.subject: BioConductor update
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

yesterday BioConductor 3.8 was released.  Usually this need upgrades of
packages in a certain sequence.  To know what package needs to be
upgraded in what sequence I've created a dependency tree[1] (you can use
the Makefile in this repository to generate a PNG).  Since I'll be busy
with real life for three weeks starting tomorrow afternoon I will not
touch this transition before end of November - but for sure every team
member is perfectly welcome to fire up routine-update[2] in the
described sequence.  If some volunteer wants to tackle this (which I'd
really welcome!) and there might be a change in the dependency tree
please also record this in the ditaa document.

Kind regards

          Andreas.

[1] https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-bioc-000-dependency-scheme/blob/master/BioC_dependency-tree.ditaa
[2] https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/maintenance-utilities/blob/master/routine-update

-- 
http://fam-tille.de

messages.subject: tidyverse package to give away
messages.body_plain:
Among the packages I maintain, readr aka r-cran-readr crept in at some point
via a reverse dependency of another package.  I have no strong affinity to
this package as I don't tend to use it myself -- and I now have a biggish
problem on my hand with it as it uses rpath (poorly).

See our bug report at
  https://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=914633
See the upstream bug report at
  https://github.com/tidyverse/readr/issues/924

Would anybody else want to take this one?

It might otherwise block the tidyverse as it fails on autopkgtests.

Thanks,  Dirk

-- 
http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com | @eddelbuettel | edd at debian.org

| in team maintenance).  Could you please clarify what package is up for

Please re-read the message.  r-cran-readr has a stupid upstream bug (which I
by now fixed).  Its bug report alreday says it would block r-cran-tidyverse
and all that package contains.  And that is what the Subject says: A
tidyverse package to give away. The body of the email is crystal-clear in its
focus on readr, and anybody who understand a little about R packages knows or
figures out how readr relates to tidyverse.

In any event, moot now as I then wasted two hours on it designing a fix.  So
currently tidyverse is not threatened by readr.

Also, don't play coy. You know there are search engines.  You also know the
pattern of package names. You know where to look up the git repo. You know we
have the QA pages.  And yet you claim you can't find it?  Ok then.

In any event, consider this offer withdrawn. I don't enjoy this email enough
to carry on the discussion. So no need to reply.

Dirk

messages.subject: Re: BioConductor update
messages.body_plain:
Hi All

What is the current status of the transition to bioconductor 3.8?

In Ubuntu I noticed some packages starting to FTBFS.
I was able to to reproduce the failures in Debian unstable [1][2][3][4][5].

Is this expected, or should I be filing bug reports?

Regards
Graham

[1] https://tests.reproducible-builds.org/debian/history/amd64/r-bioc-biomformat.html
[2] https://tests.reproducible-builds.org/debian/history/amd64/r-bioc-dnacopy.html

messages.subject: Re: BioConductor update
messages.body_plain:
Hi Graham,

This is unexpected,  I will upload in few hours a new dh-r which fix this problem.

Otherwise, the transition to bioc 3.8 is done. There are still 2 or 3 packages which did not yet reach testing.

Best,
Dylan
